q: Momentum ($p$) of a body is defined as the product of the mass of the body and its velocity.
e: True. Momentum ($p$) of a body is defined as the product of the mass of the body and its velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Momentum is written mathematically as $p = mv$.
e: True. Momentum is written mathematically as $p = mv$. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: The direction of momentum is the same as that of velocity.
e: True. The direction of momentum is the same as that of velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The unit of momentum in the MKS system is $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
e: True. The unit of momentum in the MKS system is $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: One fundamental law of physics is the law of conservation of momentum.
e: True. One fundamental law of physics is the law of conservation of momentum. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: If there is no net external force acting on an isolated system, the total momentum of the system is constant.
e: True. If there is no net external force acting on an isolated system, the total momentum of the system is constant. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest.

q: The law of conservation of momentum is true only for macroscopic objects.
e: False. Momentum conservation holds for isolated systems, microscopic as well as macroscopic. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: According to the law of conservation of momentum, total momentum before collision equals total momentum after collision.
e: True. According to the law of conservation of momentum, total momentum before collision equals total momentum after collision. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: In symbols, the conservation of momentum for two bodies is $m_A v_A + m_B v_B = m_A v'_A + m_B v'_B$.
e: True. In symbols, the conservation of momentum for two bodies is $m_A v_A + m_B v_B = m_A v'_A + m_B v'_B$. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: When a compressed spring is released between two wooden balls initially at rest, the total initial momentum is zero and so will be the final total momentum.
e: True. When a compressed spring is released between two wooden balls initially at rest, the total initial momentum is zero and so will be the final total momentum. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: The minus sign in the relation $m_B v'_B = -m_A v'_A$ indicates that the two velocity vectors are parallel and in the same direction.
e: False. The minus sign means those two velocities are opposite, not in the same direction.

q: By using the relation $m_B v'_B = m_A v'_A$ (taking magnitudes), inertial mass can be measured.
e: True. By using the relation $m_B v'_B = m_A v'_A$ (taking magnitudes), inertial mass can be measured. Inertial mass can be measured is the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.
